Explain ammonolysis and Gabriel synthesis.

body.en: Nitro compounds: $H_2$/Pd, Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl reduce $-NO_2$ to $-NH_2$ (nitrobenzene → aniline). Nitriles: $LiAlH_4$ or $H_2$/Ni gives $RCH_2NH_2$, an amine with one more carbon than the alkyl halide used to make the nitrile. Amides: $LiAlH_4$ reduces $RCONH_2$ to $RCH_2NH_2$.
body.kn: ನೈಟ್ರೋ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣ ಅನಿಲೀನ್‌ನಂತಹ ಅಮೀನ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ನೈಟ್ರೈಲ್ ಮತ್ತು ಅಮೈಡ್ ಅಪಕರ್ಷಣ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಅಮೀನ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ; ನೈಟ್ರೈಲ್ ಮಾರ್ಗ ಒಂದು ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Ammonolysis: an alkyl halide heated with ethanolic $NH_3$ gives the 1° amine, which reacts further to 2°, 3° amines and the quaternary salt $R_4N^+X^-$; excess ammonia favours the 1° amine. *Gabriel synthesis*: phthalimide + KOH → potassium phthalimide; + R–X → N-alkylphthalimide; alkaline hydrolysis → $RNH_2$ (pure 1° aliphatic amine only).

heading.en: Amines: Structure, Naming, Preparation and Physical Properties

tagline.en: Amines as derivatives of ammonia: classification, pyramidal structure, IUPAC names, the six NCERT methods of preparation and how hydrogen bonding sets their boiling points.

myth.en: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis can be used to make aniline from chlorobenzene.

truth.en: Gabriel synthesis cannot make aromatic primary amines. Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. The method looks general ("halide in, 1° amine out"). But its key step is SN2 attack on the carbon of R–X, and the C–Cl bond of chlorobenzene has partial double-bond character and sits on an sp² carbon, so it does not react.

say.en: 1°, 2°, 3° amines have one, two, three groups on N; N is sp³ and the molecule is pyramidal (about 108° in (CH₃)₃N).
Reduce nitro compounds (Fe/HCl preferred), nitriles (+1 C) or amides (same C) to make amines.
Ammonolysis gives a mixture; Gabriel gives pure 1° aliphatic amines only; Hoffmann gives one carbon fewer.
Isomeric amines boil in the order 1° > 2° > 3°; amines boil lower than alcohols of similar mass.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of methanamine is formed from 5.9 g of ethanamide by Hoffmann bromamide degradation? (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)

say.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of methanamine is formed from 5.9 grams of ethanamide by Hoffmann bromamide degradation? (C equals 12, H equals 1, N equals 14, O equals 16).
CH 3CONH 2 plus Br 2 plus 4NaOH gives CH 3NH 2 plus Na 2CO 3 plus 2NaBr plus 2H 2O (1: 1).
CH 3CONH 2 equals 24 plus 5 plus 14 plus 16 equals 59 grams per mole; 5.9 grams equals 0.1 moles.
CH 3NH 2 equals 31 grams per mole; mass equals 0.1 times 31 equals 3.1 grams.
So the answer is 3.1 grams of methanamine.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Convert bromoethane into propan-1-amine.
Need one more carbon: use the nitrile route.
CH 3CH 2Br plus KCN gives CH 3CH 2CN propanenitrile.
Reduce with LiAlH 4 (or H 2 over Ni): CH 3CH 2CH 2NH 2.
So the answer is KCN, then LiAlH 4 via propanenitrile.
